data.description:
# `rebar review` / `review_ticket` looks vestigial — decide whether it should exist

## Why this is being asked

The operator's read: if a command reviews a ticket in a SINGLE pass, it is likely vestigial, because
all plan reviews should go through the plan-review process. This ticket gathers the evidence and
forces an explicit decision rather than leaving a lightly-used LLM entry point in place by inertia.

## Evidence that it is vestigial

**No internal consumer.** `review_ticket` (`llm/operations.py`) is called by nothing inside `src/`
except its own surfaces: the CLI `review` intercept, an MCP tool (`_mcp_llm.py:46`), and the library
re-export in `llm/__init__.py`. No gate, workflow or op uses it.

**Its MCP surface is off by default.** `_mcp_llm.py:70` refuses it unless the billable-LLM-tools flag
is set: "review_ticket is disabled: it makes a live, billable LLM call."

**Not used in CI.** No workflow in `.github/workflows/` invokes `rebar review`.

**Squeezed from BELOW by free deterministic checks.** The CLI already ships `clarity-check` (scores a
ticket's clarity), `check-ac` (asserts an Acceptance Criteria block) and `quality-check` (dispatch
readiness) — all LLM-free, all exit-code-clean for scripting. Its prompt (`ticket_quality.md`) asks
for exactly this ground: "a clear problem statement and intended outcome", "an explicit, checkable
Acceptance Criteria list", "appropriate scope", "sound dependencies/ordering".

**Squeezed from ABOVE by the plan-review gate.** `review-plan` is the three-pass gate that actually
gates `claim`: ~30 criteria, a blocking DET floor, Pass-2 verification, Pass-4 coaching, a signed
attestation and a durable sidecar. Its criteria already cover clarity, ACs, scope and dependency
soundness. Anything `review` reports, the gate reports with grounding and a signature.

**Stale.** `ticket_quality.md`'s last touch was 2026-06-27, and that commit was an unrelated sweep
(container fan-out optimization) rather than a change to the reviewer.

## What WOULD be lost — state this before deciding

- a CHEAP, UNSIGNED LLM opinion on a ticket, with no DET floor to satisfy and no attestation written.
  `review-plan` on a ticket that is not claimable fast-fails by design, and it costs a full gate run;
  there is currently no "just give me a quick read on this ticket" path that uses a model.
- the `--reviewer` / `--graph` surface, which lets a caller pick a reviewer id or review a ticket
  graph as a unit. Whether anything depends on that should be checked, not assumed.
- a library entry point (`rebar.llm.review_ticket`) that external code may import. This is a public
  surface, so removal is a breaking change for library consumers.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a decision is recorded: retire, keep, or narrow. If retired, the reasoning cites what replaces
      each capability listed above
- [ ] if retired, the deprecation follows this repo's existing convention for removing a public
      surface (see `docs/deprecations.md` / the `warn_deprecated` machinery used for
      `REBAR_LLM_MODEL`), so a library consumer gets a warning before removal rather than an
      AttributeError
- [ ] if retired, the CLI intercept, the MCP tool, the library re-export, `ticket_quality.md`, and
      `select_reviewers` are all removed or explicitly kept, with each accounted for
- [ ] if KEPT, its model class is chosen deliberately (see the sibling question below) and its
      relationship to `review-plan` is documented, so the next reader does not have to re-derive
      when to use which
- [ ] usage is checked before removal, not after: search the tracker for tickets whose trail shows a
      `rebar review` invocation, and check whether any agent guidance (AGENTS.md, the packaged
      guides) tells agents to run it

## The model-class question this blocks

Ticket `afeb` routed four hand-built sub-calls onto model classes. Three were unambiguous. The fourth,
`review_ticket`, was put on `frontier` — which has a real consequence: an operator who steers with the
`llm.model` config key no longer steers `rebar review` at all. The same change deliberately LEFT
`spec_scan`'s primary call on `cfg.model`, on the reasoning that a single-call top-level op is where
`cfg.model` IS the operator's knob.

Per the operator, each one-call command should be evaluated individually rather than by a blanket
rule. If `review` is retired, its class becomes moot — which is why that decision comes first. Pending
it, the conservative interim is to leave `review_ticket` on `cfg.model` (matching `spec_scan`), since
that preserves existing operator control and is trivially reversible.

## Notes

Filed unparented: this is a product-surface question about which review paths should exist, not part
of the LLM provider seam. Raised while resolving an internal inconsistency in `afeb`.
data.title: Evaluate retiring the single-pass rebar review op: plan-review supersedes it from above, deterministic checks from below
